name: June 17, 2025 Regular Meeting
minutes_text:
MINUTES
  PARKS AND RECREATION COMMISSION
  REGULAR MEETING
  JUNE 17, 2025
  MULTIPURPOSE ROOM
  6:30 RM.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Villablanca called the meeting to order at 6:37 pm.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Judy Villablanca, Vice Chair Jake Lingo, Commissioners Georgia
  Goldfarb (arrived at 6:46 p.m.), Alicia Peak, and Dane Skophammer (arrived at 6:59 p.m.)

  ALSO PRESENT: Kristin Riesgo, Community Services Director; Tatiana Holden,
  Assistant Public Works Director; Nathaniel McLean, Assistant Engineer; Kate Manisco,
  Recreation Manager; Chris Orosz, Acting Recreation Manager; Joie Cosentino, Recreation
  Coordinator; Sebastian Spiroglou, Recreation Coordinator; Niyant Upadhyay, Recreation
  Coordinator; and Brittany Saleaumua, Administrative Assistant

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Chair Villablanca led the Pledge of Allegiance.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

  Chair Villablanca stated she wanted to reorder the agenda due t0 the number 0f
  public speakers interested in speaking on Item 5.B.

  Commissioner Peak indicated agreement and requested to hear Item 5.B. before
  Item 5.A.

  Administrative Assistant Saleaumua clarified that the agenda would be reordered
  after the Consent Calendar to hear Item 5.B., Item 5.A., Item 4.A., then Item 5.C.

MOTION  Chair Villablanca moved, and Commissioner Peak seconded a motion to approve
  the reordered agenda. The question was called, and the motion carried 3-0;
  Commissioners Goldfarb and Skophammer absent.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Administrative Assistant Saleaumua reported that the agenda for the meeting was
  posted on June 13, 2025.

ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  Introduction of Recreation Coordinators — Joie Cosentino and Niyant Upadhyay

  Community Services Director Riesgo introduced Recreation Coordinators Joie
  Cosentino and Niyant Upadhyay. She stated that Recreation Coordinator Cosentino
  would oversee the Senior Center and arts programs, and Recreation Coordinator
  Upadhyay would oversee day camps, sports, and after-school programs.

ITEM 2  WRITTEN AND ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC

  Bill Sampson advocated building a 50-meter pool at Malibu High School rather
  than a 40-meter one. He inquired ifthe Commission could work with Santa Monica-
  Malibu Unified School District to increase the pool size.

  Jo Drummond indicated agreement with Mr. Sampson’s comments and stated
  funding was needed to pay people to remove weeds at Point Dume preserve due to
  the State of California’s limited budget.

  Commissioner Goldfarb arrived at 6:46 p.m.

ITEM 3  CONSENT CALENDAR

MOTION  Chair Villablanca moved, and Vice Chair Lingo seconded a motion to approve the
  consent calendar. The question was called, and the motion carried 4-0;
  Commissioner Skophammer absent.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:
  A.  Previously Discussed Items
  None.
  B.  New Items
  A.  Approval of Minutes
  Recommended Action: Approve the minutes for the April 15, 2025 Parks
  and Recreation Commission Regular meeting.
  2.  Community Services Department Monthly Report
  Recommended Action: Receive and file a report of activities, events,
  projects,and programs coordinated by the Community Services Department
  in May 2025.

ITEM 5  NEW BUSINESS

  Pool and Swim Team Update

  Recommended Action: 1) Review the Malibu Community Pool operations and
  Swim Team programming and participation data; and 2) Provide feedback to staff.
   Parks and Recreation Commission
  Regular Meeting
  Minutes of June 17, 2025
  Page 3 of 6

Recreation Manager Manisco presented the staff report.

Speakers: Steve Reardon, Kim Ford, Liam Becker, Eli Becker, Steve Hotchkiss,
Joe Sichta, Patrick Murphree, Sue Murphree, Nina Sichta, Kim Sichta, Jo
Drummond, Erik Ran (Laura Lazar deferred time to Mr. Ran), Robert Brinkmann,
Kevin Lane, Aubree Holmes, Marc Davies, Colin Drummond (Thomas Drummond
deferred time to Mr. Drummond), Marshall Lazar, and Bill Sampson

Commissioner Skophammer arrived at 6:59 p.m.

Chair Villablanca opened the item for Commission discussion.

Commissioner Skophammer stated that any swimmer with a USA Swimming
membership was allowed to attend swim meets sanctioned by USA Swimming. He
stated that swimmers could participate individually and did not have to participate
with their Swim Team.

In response to Chair Peak, Recreation Manager Manisco stated that City lifeguards
were youth employees, and the City has struggled to recruit and hire for the
position. She stated that setting lane maximums assists with the victim response
time for the size of the surveillance zones and the time required to reach a victim,
conduct a rescue, and render care.

Commissioner Goldfarb supported sharing pool space between two swimming
organizations. She stated that employment incentives should be considered to hire
more lifeguard employees.

Chair Villablanca stated that allowing more swimmers per lane would require the
City to hire and schedule more lifeguard employees.

Commissioner Peak stated shared pool space was controversial in past discussions
between the Malibu Marlins and the Malibu Aquatics Foundation.

Vice Chair Lingo stated he reviewed participation numbers from all seasons, which
indicated that the number of swimmers was consistent. He stated he appreciated the
comments from all public speakers. He stated that not having competitive programs
could happen in a small town like Malibu, as he was facing the same issue with
Girls Softball and decided to have his daughter play in a more competitive league
in the Conejo Valley.

Commissioner Skophammer stated the Aquatics Programs Request for
Qualifications (RFQ) was released for several reasons. He stated the youth water
polo program needed pool space, and adding a second swim team was impractical
due to the limited pool space. He stated the Malibu Marlins and Malibu Aquatics

Foundation had different program philosophies, and one group should not be
blamed for swimmers dropping out of the swim team.

Commissioner Peak encouraged the Malibu Marlins to offer a competitive
sw1mm1ng program.

Chair Villablanca stated the two swimming organizations could not share the pool
and wanted to discuss lifeguard recruitment at a future meeting.

The Commission requested staff to provide an update on swim team participation
and lifeguard recruitment.

In response to Commissioner Skophammer, Community Services Director Riesgo
stated the Commission would review the RFQ process at a future meeting.

Chair Villablanca thanked the public for their time and comments.

Malibu Bluffs Park Snack Shack

Recommended Action: l) Receive a presentation on the conceptual design of the
Malibu Bluffs Park Snack Shack; and 2) Provide feedback to staff regarding the
design.

Community Services Director Riesgo presented the staff report and introduced Jun
Fujita Hall, the Principal Project Architect working with the Public Works
Department on the Snack Shack project.

Ms. Fujita Hall presented the Snack Shack conceptual design.

Speaker: Bill Sampson

Commissioner Skophammer suggested moving the building towards Winter Mesa
Road to allow more space in front of the building.

Commissioner Peak expressed her concerns about the drainage surrounding the
Snack Shack.

Vice Chair Lingo preferred shifting the building toward Winter Mesa Road and
adding a retaining wall. He stated the slope could not be utilized and suggested the
consultant provide a cost estimate for the revised work.

Commissioner Skophammer requested to shift the building east towards the
Michael Landon Center.

ITEM 4  OLD BUSINESS

  Jake Kurediian Citizenship Award

  Recommended Action: 1) Review and discuss the nominations for the 2025 Jake
  Kuredjian Citizenship Award; and 2) Select one or more nominees for City Council
  consideration.

  Community Services Director Riesgo presented the staff report.

  Public Speakers: Bill Sampson, Jo Drummond, and Colin Drummond

  The Commission discussed whether to nominate two or three nominees.

  Chair Villablanca stated based on the Commission’s feedback, three nominations
  should be considered.

MOTION  Commissioner Peak moved, and Commissioner Goldfarb seconded a motion to
  recommend Suzanne Guldimann, Andy Lyon, and Nick Shurgot for City Council
  consideration for the 2025 Jake Kuredjian Citizenship Award. The question was
  called, and the motion carried unanimously.

ITEM 5  NEW BUSINESS

  Trancas Canyon Park Field Renovation

  Recommended Action: Review and provide feedback regarding the timing of the
  annual field renovation at Trancas Canyon Park.

  Acting Recreation Manager Orosz presented the staff report.

  In response to Vice Chair Lingo, Acting Recreation Manager Orosz stated the
  annual field renovation at Trancas Canyon Park would have less impact on the
  soccer leagues and programs in the Spring.

  In response to Commissioner Skophammer, Acting Recreation Manager Orosz
  stated installing sod would still require a field closure and there would be additional
  costs. He stated Winter renovations would conflict with the Malibu Bluffs Park
  multipurpose field renovation.

MOTION  Chair Villablanca moved, and Commissioner Peak seconded a motion to conduct
  the Trancas Canyon Park annual field renovation during the Spring season, aligning
  the time with Santa Monica—Malibu Unified School District Spring Break. The
  question was called, and the motion carried unanimously.

ITEM 6  STAFF UPDATES

  Acting Recreation Manager Orosz provided an update on Charmlee Wilderness
  Park trail maintenance and Day Camps.

  Recreation Manager Manisco provided an update on Aquatics programs.

  Community Services Director Riesgo provided an update on Senior Center
  programs, Parks and Recreation month, and the Commission meeting schedule.

CONSENSUS
  By Consensus? the Commission cancelled the July 15. 2025, Regular meeting and
  scheduled a Special meeting on July 29, 2025.

ITEM 7  COMMISSIONER REPORTS, COMMENTS AND INQUIRIES

  Vice Chair Lingo thanked staff for their assistance on Malibu Little League Closing
  Day.

  In response to Commissioner Peak, Recreation Manager Manisco stated the cost to
  build and operate a 50—meter pool versus a 40—meter pool was significant.

FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  Lifeguard Recruitment
  Review the Request for Qualifications Process

ADJOURNMENT

  Chair Villablanca adjourned the meeting at 9:32 p.m.

  Approved and adopted by the Parks and
  Recreation Commission of the City of
  Malibuo July 29,2025.
